title: Need for zkSpeed: Accelerating HyperPlonk for Zero-Knowledge Proofs
problem: Generating zero-knowledge proofs using the HyperPlonk zkSNARK protocol is prohibitively slow on CPUs, requiring minutes to hours, due to its four heterogeneous proof phases that demand large-bitwidth (255-381 bit) modular arithmetic over polynomials of degree up to 2^24. Existing ZKP accelerators target simpler protocols (Groth16, Orion, Spartan) that either require per-application trusted setups or produce large proofs, leaving HyperPlonk—which avoids both pitfalls—unaccelerated.
motivation: HyperPlonk's combination of universal trusted setup and small proof sizes makes it ideal for blockchain and verifiable ML applications, but its prover workload is dominated by bandwidth-intensive SumCheck and compute-intensive Multi-Scalar Multiplication (MSM) kernels that require specialized hardware to be viable.
method: zkSpeed is a specialized computer chip with eight processing units that work together to generate zero-knowledge proofs—cryptographic proofs that demonstrate knowledge of information without revealing it. It performs massive multiplication on very large numbers (255-381 bits) using polynomial structures up to degree 2^24 (roughly 16 million); one unit cuts multiplication time by 92% through improved value grouping, and another processes operations in batches of 64 to spread out the cost of expensive calculations. The units communicate through four shared channels; polynomial data is compressed 10-11 times to fit in fast on-chip memory, while large computation streams use high-bandwidth memory at 2 TB/s. The design was optimized by simulating thousands of chip configurations.
key_novelty: The core innovation is fitting the complete HyperPlonk proving process into a single chip by reusing hardware—a circuit that performs all three proof checks (ZeroCheck, PermCheck, OpenCheck) using shared multipliers to cut area by 48.9%, combined with a hybrid tree-traversal unit and batched division operations.
contributions: A fully-pipelined unified SumCheck accelerator supporting all three HyperPlonk SumCheck polynomial structures with 48.9% area reduction via modular multiplier sharing.
A novel modular inversion architecture using constant-time BEEA with Montgomery batching (batch size 64) and multiplier tree, reducing latency imbalance and enabling one inversion output per cycle.
A Multifunction Tree Unit with hybrid DFS/BFS traversal eliminating full-level intermediate storage, saving 41.6% area across Pareto design points vs. dedicated units.
A full-chip design-space exploration (thousands of configurations) showing 801x geomean speedup over CPU (AMD EPYC 7502) at iso-compute area with a 366mm2, 7nm chip and 2 TB/s HBM.

metrics.speedup: 801x geomean over AMD EPYC 7502 CPU at iso-compute area (366mm2, 2 TB/s HBM)
metrics.other: 48.9% area saved on SumCheck PE via multiplier sharing; 92% reduction in MSM bucket aggregation latency; 41.6% area saved via Multifunction Tree unit reuse; 10-11x on-chip MLE compression

limitations: Evaluation uses synthetically generated mock circuits (no real application compiler for HyperPlonk exists), so workload diversity is limited; the accelerator is ASIC-only with fixed protocol support.
primary_theme: ASIC acceleration of zero-knowledge proof generation
